download_card_image.description: Download one of a card's images and store it, so a later step can attach it to an email, post it or put it in a document. Choose the whole rendered card, the square art at either size, the lossless original or the deck-list tile. Asking for a render of a card the service does not pre-render comes back as a sentence naming what to ask for instead, rather than as a 404. HearthstoneJSON asks that busy sites re-host rather than hotlink, which is what this action is for. No API key required.

get_card.description: Get one Hearthstone card in full, by its name, its card ID or its dbfId: 'Leeroy Jenkins', 'EX1_116' and 559 all find the same card. Every field the game publishes comes back, from the rules text and the flavour joke to the play requirements and the pool a card creates from, along with every image URL. A card the collectible set does not hold, such as a hero power or an enchantment, is looked for in the whole game rather than reported missing. No API key required.

get_enum_values.description: Read the enumerations behind the card data. Every set code, class, card type, rarity, minion type and game tag is one member of one of these, so this is where a value the filters did not offer comes from, and how a number in another Hearthstone tool is turned back into a name. Leave the enumeration empty to see which ones the service publishes. No API key required.

get_latest_build.description: Find out which game build HearthstoneJSON is publishing right now, how many collectible cards and sets it holds, and which sets are newest. The build number is what pins the rest of a workflow to one patch, so every step reads the same cards even if a patch lands mid-run, and comparing it against a build recorded earlier is how a workflow notices that a new expansion is out. No API key required.

get_random_card.description: Pick a card at random out of everything the filters leave, or a handful of them. The filters are the ones Search cards takes, so a step can ask for a random Legendary from one expansion, or a random Murloc, rather than a random anything. Built for the workflows that post a card of the day or open a meeting with one. An empty pool is reported as found: false with the filters that produced it, rather than as a failed step. No API key required.

get_related_cards.description: Get the cards one card brings with it: the pool it creates from, the hero power a hero comes with, and the tokens and enchantments it summons or applies. Nothing in the card data links those last ones, so they are found through the game's own ID convention, which is what turns 'Leeroy Jenkins' into the 1/1 Whelps he gives your opponent. Reads the whole game, since none of these are collectible. No API key required.

search_cards.description: Search every Hearthstone card by text and by every property a card has: set, class, type, rarity, minion type, spell school, keyword, mana cost, attack and health. Each card comes back with its rules text in plain form, its keywords spelled out, and its art, tile and render URLs already built, so a step can post a card without a second call. This is the action to reach for first: it turns 'legendary Dragon minions that cost seven or less' into the cards themselves. Reads the collectible set unless told otherwise. No API key required.

description: Read Hearthstone's card data from a workflow. HearthstoneJSON publishes every card in the game, converted straight out of the game files, in fourteen languages. Search the whole card pool by text and by set, class, type, rarity, minion type, spell school, keyword, mana cost, attack and health; look one card up by name, ID or dbfId; pick one at random for a card of the day; and follow a card to the tokens, enchantments and hero power it brings with it. Break a slice of the pool down by every property at once, with its mana curve and its averages, to see what an expansion gave each class. Every card comes back with its rules text in plain readable form and its art, tile and full-card render already addressed, and any of those images can be downloaded and attached. The card sets, minion types, spell schools and keywords a step can filter on are read from the card data itself, so a new expansion needs no new setup. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
